plan.scenario: When a user wants to cancel a flight reservation and asks for help with bookings
plan.experience: Gather and verify the user's reservations and full booking details, then systematically check each candidate against all cancellation eligibility conditions (booked within 24 hours, airline cancelled, business cabin, or insurance covering the stated reason) before denying ineligible requests with clear reasons or proceeding. Require explicit user confirmation before calling any cancel API, explain refund timelines afterward, and refuse unauthorized exceptions, vouchers, or partial refunds while offering human-agent transfer if the user insists on escalation.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a flight date change on a reservation that may be in a non-modifiable fare class or has special circumstances (e.g., bereavement).
plan.experience: Plan to first retrieve full reservation details (fare class, segments, whether any flight has flown), then apply modification policy gates (basic economy cannot be modified; flown segments cannot be modified). If ineligible, deny clearly and offer human-agent transfer for exception/escalation requests rather than promising changes.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a cabin upgrade for all passengers plus baggage additions on an existing reservation.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve reservation and user details first, verify membership level and passenger count, check that no segment has flown and that cabin changes apply uniformly to all passengers and segments, compute the price difference, verify baggage allowance and fees, and require explicit confirmation before any update. If the user's budget is below the full-upgrade cost, offer compliant alternatives such as keeping the current cabin and adding bags, or checking other flights.

plan.scenario: When a user requests cancellation of a flight reservation and asks whether a refund is available.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve full reservation details, ask for the cancellation reason, then check every refund-eligibility condition (booking age, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance coverage for the stated reason) before deciding. Require explicit confirmation before any cancel call, and if ineligible, clearly deny and offer human-agent transfer without promising exceptions.

plan.scenario: When a user asks for the reason behind a flight delay and/or compensation, and the available tools may only return status without a reason.
plan.experience: Plan to first check whether a flight-status tool exists and query it for the specific flight and date; if the tool returns only status without a reason, explicitly plan to state that the reason is unavailable through agent tools and offer human-agent transfer. Do not invent a cause. For compensation, plan to confirm facts and apply policy gates only if the user asks, and avoid proactively promising vouchers or refunds.

plan.scenario: When a user requests flight cancellation with a refund and the request may be ineligible.
plan.experience: Plan to collect user id and reservation id, obtain the cancellation reason, retrieve full reservation details, and systematically check every eligibility condition (booked within 24 hours, airline cancelled, business cabin, insurance covering the stated reason) before deciding. Plan to deny ineligible requests with specific failing conditions, refuse exceptions uniformly, offer human-agent transfer if the user insists, and never call the cancel API without eligibility and explicit confirmation.

plan.scenario: When a user requests multiple simultaneous reservation changes (flight dates/routing, cabin upgrade, baggage additions) with a budget constraint.
plan.experience: Before making any update, retrieve the full reservation and user details, enumerate all policy constraints that could block the request (cabin uniformity across all segments/passengers, no splitting, baggage add-only, no origin/destination change, no miles/promos), and search all available fare options to compute the true minimum total cost including cabin and baggage effects. Compare that total against the user's stated budget and, if it exceeds the cap, clearly explain why and present compliant alternatives (e.g., keep current cabin and add bags, or upgrade all segments) rather than partially applying changes or promising exceptions. Require explicit confirmation before any update API call.

plan.scenario: When a user requests flight cancellation with refund citing illness and claims insurance was purchased.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve full reservation details, verify insurance status from the record rather than user claims, check all eligibility conditions (booking age, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance coverage for stated reason), deny with specific failing conditions if ineligible, and offer human-agent transfer when the user insists.

plan.scenario: When a user requests compensation for a delayed flight but does not want to change or cancel the reservation.
plan.experience: Plan to verify the reservation and flight status, then apply the compensation policy gate strictly: a delay certificate requires the user to change or cancel the reservation, so if the user refuses, deny compensation with the specific failing condition and offer human-agent transfer if they insist on an exception. Do not plan to promise refunds to original payment method or goodwill vouchers outside policy.

plan.scenario: When a user reports a flight delay but the available tools only return current flight status and cannot confirm historical delays or provide a reason.
plan.experience: Plan to check the status of all relevant flight segments, explicitly state that the delay cannot be verified with available tools, avoid inventing a cause, and offer human-agent transfer for investigation. Apply compensation and change/cancel policy gates only if the user asks, and do not promise compensation without verified facts.

plan.scenario: When a user asks to remove a passenger from an existing multi-passenger reservation.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve the reservation, verify the named passenger exists, and check the policy that passenger modifications cannot change the total passenger count. If removal would reduce the count, deny clearly and offer alternatives (e.g., cabin change, human-agent transfer) rather than attempting an unsupported edit.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a passenger name change on an existing reservation.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve reservation details first to identify passengers and verify the passenger count, collect the target passenger and new name/DOB, confirm the passenger count remains unchanged, present the exact edit for explicit confirmation, then update only after confirmation.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a flight change (date and/or cabin) and is open to alternate destinations or connections.
plan.experience: Plan to first retrieve the full reservation to confirm fare class, segments, and whether any segment has flown; then apply modification policy gates (Basic Economy and flown segments are ineligible; origin, destination, and trip type must remain unchanged, so reject alternate destinations even if the user suggests them). Plan to search both direct and one-stop options for the target date in the requested cabin, compare total fares, and require explicit user confirmation before calling the update tool, including the refund/payment method.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a refund for an add-on (e.g., travel insurance) while keeping the underlying booking.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve the reservation to confirm the add-on was purchased, check the policy for whether add-ons can be removed or refunded independently, deny clearly citing the specific rule if not permitted, avoid any update/cancel API call, and offer human-agent transfer only if the user insists or requests escalation.

plan.scenario: When a user asks about baggage allowance and disputes their membership level or other profile data.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve both user profile and reservation details, compute allowance from the system-recorded membership and cabin class, clearly state the recorded value, and offer human-agent transfer if the user insists the data is incorrect. Do not override system data based on user claims.

plan.scenario: When a user requests multiple flight actions (cancellations and a modification) in one session.
plan.experience: Plan to handle each reservation independently: retrieve full details, ask for cancellation reasons, check every eligibility condition (24-hour window, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance coverage), verify flown status via flight status tools, and for modifications confirm origin/destination/trip type unchanged, cabin not basic economy, and no segment flown. Require explicit confirmation before any booking update, deny ineligible requests with specific reasons, and offer human transfer for out-of-scope or flown reservations.

plan.scenario: When a user requests compensation for a missed meeting or general inconvenience after claiming an airline-canceled flight.
plan.experience: Plan to verify the claimed reservation against the user's actual bookings before discussing compensation; check cabin class, flight status, membership level, and insurance. Plan to apply the policy gate (compensation only for airline-canceled flights when silver/gold, insured, or business cabin, as a per-passenger certificate) and to explicitly state that missed meetings and inconvenience are not compensable. Plan to escalate to a human agent if the user insists on out-of-policy compensation.

plan.scenario: When a user asks to cancel multiple upcoming reservations filtered by a passenger-count criterion (e.g., only one passenger).
plan.experience: Plan to first resolve the user and enumerate their reservations, filter to the requested subset (upcoming and matching passenger count), then for each candidate gather the cancellation reason and systematically verify every eligibility condition (booking age, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance coverage for the stated reason, and no already-flown segments) before denying with specific failing conditions or proceeding; require explicit confirmation before any cancel call and offer human-agent transfer only if the user insists.

plan.scenario: When a user suspects duplicate or overlapping flight bookings and asks for help sorting them out.
plan.experience: Plan to first obtain the user ID, retrieve all reservations, and compare dates/routes/passengers to identify overlaps. Then clarify the user's actual travel plans to determine which bookings to keep vs. cancel. For any cancellation, plan to check all eligibility conditions (booking age, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance coverage for stated reason) and verify no segments have flown before proceeding. Require explicit confirmation before any cancellation API call and explain refund timelines afterward.

plan.scenario: When a user asks to cancel all upcoming reservations and is willing to forgo refunds, including bookings that fail refund-eligibility conditions.
plan.experience: Separate the refund-eligibility decision from the cancellation decision: eligibility gates (24-hour window, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance) determine refunds, not whether a cancellation can be processed. Plan to cancel any not-yet-flown reservation the user explicitly confirms, even without refund, and reserve denial/human transfer only for already-flown segments or cases where the cancel tool itself rejects the request. Do not treat cabin class as a blanket cancellation permission.

plan.scenario: When a requested modification is denied due to fare-class ineligibility and the user asks to book a new reservation instead.
plan.experience: Plan the fallback booking path explicitly: after denying the modification, if the user opts to book anew, include steps to verify membership level and baggage allowance for the new fare, confirm passenger details, select payment method, and obtain explicit confirmation of all details (flight, cabin, bags, fees, total) before calling the booking tool. Do not assume membership tier or free-bag counts without checking.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a destination change (e.g., LGA to JFK) on an existing reservation and cites trip insurance for fee waivers.
plan.experience: Plan to first determine whether the requested change is a modification (origin/destination/trip type must stay the same) or requires cancel-and-rebook. If cancel-and-rebook, verify insurance status and coverage eligibility from the reservation record before proposing cancellation; do not treat user claims of insurance as sufficient. Explicitly plan to check whether the insurance actually covers the stated reason and whether cancellation is permitted, and present the cancellation as conditional on that verification.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a flight cancellation/refund citing a personal emergency and may be ineligible, and may escalate to date changes or adding insurance.
plan.experience: Plan to gather user and reservation IDs, confirm the reason category, retrieve full reservation details, and systematically check every eligibility condition (booked within 24 hours, airline cancelled, business cabin, insurance covering the reason) before deciding. Anticipate follow-on requests (date change, adding insurance) and plan to evaluate them against policy too. Deny ineligible requests with specific failing conditions, refuse exceptions uniformly, respect a no-transfer request, and never call the cancel API without eligibility and explicit confirmation.

exec.scenario: When checking cancellation eligibility for one or more reservations
exec.experience: Retrieve full reservation details for all candidate bookings, use get_flight_status on each segment to verify no portion has flown (denying cancellation and transferring to a human if landed), and evaluate each against every cancellation condition using actual booking date, cabin class, insurance status, and stated reason. Present a clear eligibility assessment with specific conditions met/failed; if ineligible, do not cancel (even if the user waives refund), explain that rules apply uniformly without exceptions, respect the user's decision to keep the reservation, offer to check an alternative booking the user identifies, and offer escalation only if the user insists. For eligible bookings, obtain explicit user confirmation, then call cancel_reservation for each approved booking and confirm results and refund details afterward; for modification requests, search direct flights for the exact origin, destination, and date, and if none exist, report that clearly and offer alternative dates or one-stop options rather than proceeding with an invalid change.

exec.scenario: When evaluating time-based eligibility conditions such as a 24-hour cancellation window
exec.experience: Explicitly compute the elapsed time between the booking timestamp and the current time before claiming a time-based condition is met; do not assume 'booked recently' means within the window. If the condition fails and no other condition (airline cancellation, eligible cabin, insurance) holds, deny the cancellation instead of proceeding.

exec.scenario: When a user pushes for exceptions, vouchers, or partial refunds after an ineligible cancellation is denied
exec.experience: Hold the policy line: do not issue vouchers, gift cards, partial or goodwill refunds, and do not claim supervisor overrides; explain rules apply uniformly, then offer and perform a transfer to a human agent if the user requests escalation.

exec.scenario: When booking a reservation with a specified payment method (e.g., a particular card brand) after applying stored credits/certificates
exec.experience: Before calling book_reservation, look up the exact payment_method id in the user's profile matching the stated brand and last four digits, and pass that id with the correct remainder amount after confirming the payment breakdown and card identity with the user. Never substitute a different stored card id; if the named card cannot be found, stop and confirm with the user rather than guessing.

exec.scenario: When a user requests a modification that policy forbids but pleads for an exception due to hardship.
exec.experience: Retrieve reservation details to confirm the fare class and eligibility, explain the specific policy reason for denial, and when the user insists on an exception, transfer to a human agent with a summary including reservation id, route, fare class, passenger count, and the stated reason—without calling any modify API.

exec.scenario: When a user asks to upgrade only one passenger or otherwise partially change cabin class on a multi-passenger reservation.
exec.experience: Enforce cabin uniformity across all passengers and segments by clearly denying partial cabin changes with the reason, then offer compliant alternatives (e.g., full upgrade cost vs. keep economy and add bags). Recompute the price difference using current reservation and searched flight prices, verify baggage fees against membership/cabin allowance, and proceed only after explicit user confirmation. Use the correct update tool (update_reservation_flights or update_reservation_baggages) with the confirmed parameters and the correct payment_id from the profile.

exec.scenario: When a user reports a delayed flight and asks why it happened, and the status tool returns only a status value.
exec.experience: Call the flight-status tool with the flight number and date, report exactly what the tool returns, and clearly state that the reason is not available if the tool does not provide it. Offer a human-agent transfer for the reason. If the user also requests compensation, transfer with a summary of the request rather than promising any compensation yourself.

exec.scenario: When executing a cancellation-eligibility check and the user repeatedly demands an exception or full refund.
exec.experience: Retrieve reservation and user details, confirm no segment has flown via get_flight_status, and evaluate each eligibility condition against actual booking date, cabin class, insurance status, and stated reason, stating the specific failing conditions. Hold the denial consistently across repeated requests, explain rules apply uniformly without exceptions, respect the user's choice not to be transferred, and leave the reservation unchanged. For date-change requests, search flights for the exact route/date and report availability without modifying basic-economy bookings, and explain that insurance cannot be added after booking.

exec.scenario: When a user asks to list their other upcoming flights or total costs after a cancellation/escalation request
exec.experience: Before reporting reservations as belonging to the user, confirm each reservation's user_id matches the verified user (and that passengers are the user or their companions); only include reservations that pass ownership verification, and exclude already-flown segments from 'upcoming' totals. If ownership cannot be confirmed, state that rather than presenting the bookings as the user's.

exec.scenario: When executing a bundled change request where the user has set a maximum acceptable total cost.
exec.experience: Search each requested leg separately, compute the net price difference from original segment prices, verify baggage fees against cabin/membership allowance (free bags may reduce cost), and if the computed total exceeds the user's stated limit, do not call any update tool—clearly report the breakdown and confirm the reservation remains unchanged.

exec.scenario: When a user insists insurance was purchased but the record shows none, and demands escalation.
exec.experience: Re-verify the reservation record on request, state the system's insurance status clearly, hold the denial consistently without promising exceptions, and honor the user's request to transfer to a human agent with a concise summary of the dispute.

exec.scenario: When a user claims a membership tier that conflicts with the profile record and demands an exception for compensation.
exec.experience: Report the membership level as shown in the system without overriding it, state the specific policy condition that blocks compensation, and when the user insists on an out-of-policy exception, transfer to a human agent with a summary of the verified facts and the refused request rather than inventing goodwill credits.

exec.scenario: When a user reports a delay on a specific reservation but cannot provide the exact flight number or date, and the system shows all segments as available.
exec.experience: Check the status of every segment on the reservation, report the results transparently, explain that the delay cannot be confirmed with available tools, and offer to transfer to a human agent for further investigation. Do not fabricate a delay or compensation offer.

exec.scenario: When a user pivots from a denied passenger removal to a cabin downgrade with refund on a multi-passenger reservation.
exec.experience: Search current fares for the same flights and cabin, compute the new total for all passengers, subtract from the original amount paid to determine the refund, present the breakdown, obtain explicit confirmation, then call update_reservation_flights with the correct cabin, flight numbers/dates, and payment_id from the user profile. Confirm the update and refund afterward.

exec.scenario: When executing a confirmed passenger name change on a reservation.
exec.experience: Call get_reservation_details to obtain the current passenger list, then after explicit user confirmation call update_reservation_passengers with the full passenger array preserving unchanged passengers and only altering the confirmed fields; verify the tool result reflects the change.

exec.scenario: When executing a flight change after the plan has confirmed eligibility and the user has approved a specific new itinerary.
exec.experience: Search both direct and one-stop flights for the target date, filter to the requested cabin (exclude Basic Economy), compute total fares per itinerary, and present the cheapest options with routing and times. After explicit confirmation, call update_reservation_flights with the confirmed cabin, flight numbers/dates, and the payment_id from the user profile; then report the new itinerary, fare, and refund amount.

exec.scenario: When a user insists on a change that violates policy or exceeds their budget after initial pricing.
exec.experience: Exhaustively search all available flight/fare combinations (direct and one-stop, flexible times) to confirm the minimum cost, recompute totals for all passengers, and if the constraint still cannot be met, state the limitation clearly with the cheapest valid option and offer alternatives; do not fabricate discounts or split reservations.

exec.scenario: When a user asks for the fastest available connecting itinerary and the search returns multiple one-stop combinations.
exec.experience: Compute total travel time from departure to final arrival for every candidate combination, including layover, and rank strictly by that total. Do not discard a candidate merely because its computed layover is short unless you have verified the connection is infeasible; if a connection is too tight, exclude it explicitly and then pick the next-fastest by total duration. Present the true fastest realistic option first and confirm it matches the user's request before booking.

exec.scenario: When a user disputes profile information (e.g., membership level) that affects policy-based calculations.
exec.experience: Double-check the profile via the appropriate tool, clearly state the system-recorded value, explain that calculations are based on that value, and if the user remains insistent, transfer to a human agent with a summary of the discrepancy rather than altering the data.

exec.scenario: When a user claims a canceled flight but cannot provide a booking code and no matching reservation appears on their profile.
exec.experience: Retrieve all reservations for the verified user, filter to those matching the claimed date/cabin, and use get_flight_status on each candidate segment to confirm whether it was actually canceled. Report the concrete findings (no business-class booking, segments landed) and the specific policy failing conditions, then transfer to a human agent if the user insists on escalation rather than fabricating a booking or promising compensation.

exec.scenario: When booking a new reservation after a denied modification.
exec.experience: Before calling book_reservation, verify the user's membership level and the actual checked-bag allowance for the chosen cabin; compute nonfree_baggages correctly rather than asserting bags are free. Confirm all booking parameters (flight, date, cabin, passenger DOB, payment amount) with the user, then call book_reservation with accurate total_baggages and nonfree_baggages.

exec.scenario: When executing a cancel-and-rebook flow under trip insurance for a health reason.
exec.experience: Before calling cancel_reservation, verify the reservation's insurance status and eligibility conditions from retrieved data; if insurance is not confirmed on the record, do not cancel—instead inform the user and offer alternatives or human-agent transfer. After cancellation, confirm refund details and only then proceed to booking.
